R-COMPARE-BUNDLE-NOUN-PHRASES: BLOCK_RELEVANCE_POLICY uses _has_bundle_phrase_prefix and _has_bundle_phrase_suffix in the shared _positive_marker_text path for titles and queries. The prefix helper walks backwards from one accessory through at most three whitespace-adjacent _BUNDLE_MODIFIER words (material/type/color adjectives or connector names), then requires the original explicit 'with [a/an]' or 'в комплекте' cue with its optional colon/dash. The unchanged suffix helper extends one accessory through at most three recognized modifiers or head-specific noun complements, allowing a noun complement once, then requires 'в комплекте'. Unknown words, punctuation inside the phrase, unrelated nouns, relation words and another accessory stop extension; only the original marker occurrence is masked. The immediate bundle and direct-negation rules and raw ranking are unchanged. Code-bound execution and its negative controls are recorded in V-M-COMPARE and evidence/latest.json; this architecture note does not replace source or runtime evidence.

flow.steps: MCP client sends initialize/tools/list/tools/call and resources/list/resources/read through stdio or configured HTTP; runtime selects serving transport and exposure policy; native or unified server validates tool arguments, selects an upstream route, parses data and returns typed content or structured ToolError. Unified mounting preserves native names and records skipped imports, MARKETPLACE_SOURCES deselections and a connector's own credential-gate reason (MPStats without MPSTATS_MP_AUTH). Which sources exist at all is stated once in the source registry (M-SOURCES); the mount table, the capability table, the CLI config/selfcheck rows, the unblock map, compare's source list and the CI inventory read it or are pinned to it by a parity test. Each server publishes the reference half of its tool descriptions as resources: guide://<source>/<tool> per tool, with the tool description naming the same URI, and one marketplace://errors built from the error taxonomy; the initialize instructions say so in one line. mount_child hides a mounted child's copy of the shared URI, so a profile lists it once while the child keeps it for standalone use (R-TOOL-RESOURCES). marketplace_sources adds the needs_cdp set, which follows each mounted source's effective route (R-CDP-CAPABILITY-TRUTH), and marketplace_health answers CDP reachability, the shared navigation budget, retained handoffs and the unblock page per mounted source from local state only: it spends no navigation, starts no Chrome and opens or closes no tab (R-TRANSPORT-HEALTH).
flow.read: Console entrypoint and connector modules; MCP_TRANSPORT/MCP_HTTP_* environment; MARKETPLACE_SOURCES; MPSTATS_MP_AUTH for the MPStats mount gate; CHROME_CDP_HOST/CHROME_CDP_PORT and the CDP HTTP endpoints for marketplace_health; JSON-RPC arguments. No client configuration file is read by the server itself.
flow.write: JSON-RPC stdout for stdio or HTTP responses; stderr diagnostics. No application data file is written by mounting/introspection, and resource reads only return text already held in the module.
flow.handoff: DF-HTTP or DF-CDP then DF-PARSE. marketplace_sources describes loaded/static capabilities, not live source health; marketplace_health reads transport state only and proves no marketplace is up. Selfchecks remain operator-only. Guides and the error reference are reference text, never live data.

flow.steps: Tool assembles validated public API/SSR request; connector pacing/cache and bounded HTTP read constrain traffic and body size. Shared GET helpers return status/text for connector classification; the impersonated curl_cffi tier-1 read whose streamed body is capped and decoded is the shared M-KIT one, behind each connector's own module-level wrapper. Ozon runs impersonated blocking HTTP in an allowlisted worker; some connectors implement their own transport and fallback policy. Lamoda cards try HTTP GraphQL first (tier 1); HTTP 200 skips CDP, while a non-200 response or httpx.TransportError triggers exactly one in-page GraphQL POST through operator Chrome over CDP (tier 2), reporting tier_used graphql_cdp on success. Dated reason: 2026-10-12 GraphQL over HTTPS returned a 307 loop. MPStats reads analytics with its optional token.
flow.read: Connector settings/environment and proxy configuration; upstream HTTPS response bytes; in-memory cache. MPSTATS_MP_AUTH is read from environment for the documented optional API exception.
flow.write: In-memory cache/pacer counters and stderr events; no shared HTTP cache file. Ozon worker communication uses process pipes; worker-tree cleanup is an OS side effect, not a marketplace write.
flow.handoff: Lamoda card non-200 or httpx.TransportError hands off once to DF-CDP for an in-page GraphQL POST; successful fallback sets tier_used graphql_cdp. Other refusals may trigger connector-specific CDP fallback, not universal fallback for every source. Shared budgeted helper enters its supplied limiter before retries only; preserve this observed behavior rather than infer first-attempt pacing.

flow.steps: Tool uses browser-fetch or rendered DOM/state appropriate to its connector; connect to operator Chrome, autostart only for loopback, acquire the navigation budget's host slot before the global one (an open host breaker is refused before and after queuing), create an owned target, navigate within host policy, evaluate the read/extractor, classify walls and return raw content. The render-one-page-and-parse-JSON step, its pacing call and its lock are the shared assembly in M-KIT; a connector keeps a module-level wrapper under the name its tests patch. Use Playwright or raw-CDP fallback; cleanup closes the owned target unless an explicit handoff retains it. A Taobao search grid that is still rendering is re-read in the SAME owned page for a bounded while (no second navigation, no waiting on a login or CAPTCHA wall).
flow.read: CHROME_CDP_HOST/PORT, CHROME_BINARY, CHROME_SCRAPING_PROFILE, CHROME_NAV_TIMEOUT_MS and budget knobs; AliExpress supplies ALI_TIMEOUT as its source override; browser session through CDP; public marketplace page/API content. Application code does not open browser cookie databases.
flow.write: Autostart may create P-CHROME; Chrome itself owns profile/session storage. Browser tab/navigation/window state and in-memory budget diagnostics change; ordinary extraction/snapshots do not write page content or images to disk.
flow.handoff: AliExpress card reads use a search landing and an in-page card tab; WB_TRANSPORT=dom affects only WB search/cards. Authentication and anti-bot success are not verified by static inspection.

flow.steps: HTTP status/text or CDP payload enters source-specific JSON/SSR/DOM parser; tolerant aliases/coercion retain missing values as None, collect warnings and distinguish shape drift from transport refusal. Construct source response models/meta and serialize public MCP content; schema compaction changes advertised shape only, not the response model.
flow.read: Upstream payload in memory; source parser/shape-reference constants where implemented; model definitions. Shape-reference Python constants are code, not a runtime fixture file.
flow.write: Typed responses, warnings and metadata in memory; ToolError JSON and redacted diagnostics on failure. No parser output file is written by normal tool calls.

flow.steps: compare_prices validates source selection, fans out concurrently with asyncio.gather and a per-source wait_for ceiling, normalizes source-native results, deduplicates listings and returns partial SourceOutcome records. Rank usable everyday RUB prices only, retaining missing/native-currency offers without inventing exchange rates. R-COMPARE-CONDITIONAL-PRICE preserves optional price_kind and conditional-only quoted amounts in price_native, excludes marked conditions from both winners, uses a source-provided everyday price rather than a struck/reference price, and warns with each known conditional amount and condition. R-COMPARE-VARIANT-IDENTITY extracts normalised GB/ГБ and TB/ТБ sizes from the query and each title before choosing cheapest_comparable: a title naming sizes and none of them an asked size keeps its rank and may stay plain cheapest but is never the like-for-like candidate, and one identity_mismatch warning per call names the excluded offers and the sizes. Detsky Mir has card support but no text search; Cian/MPStats do not participate in goods-search comparison. compare_verify_offer re-reads a native card for price/stock/identity; decision_inspect exposes native card inspection via the separate five-tool decision profile.
flow.read: MARKETPLACE_SOURCES, COMPARE_SOURCE_TIMEOUT; installed source modules; in-memory upstream offers and selected product identifiers; identity/model definitions.
flow.write: CompareResponse, per-source warnings/failures and verification records in memory; stderr events; underlying DF-HTTP/DF-CDP side effects only.

flow.steps: When enabled, retain an owned challenge page in a bounded process-local lease keyed by exact client scope/operation/URL/CDP endpoint/profile (current_client_scope: the MCP session on handshake-era connections; the stdio process on sessionless 2026-07-28 stdio connections; none, so no retention, on sessionless HTTP or in-memory connections and outside a request); surface opaque handoff metadata, then repeat the same read after operator action without searching unrelated tabs or navigating anew. Keep immutable lifetime and idle bounds, content digest/resume notes and closure on expiry/shutdown. compare_browser_snapshot checks ownership/liveness and image-delivery policy before returning bounded viewport pixels or text guidance.
flow.read: CHROME_CHALLENGE_HANDOFF_* knobs, negotiated protocol era, transport and session identity, lease registry and owned page; client capability/vision policy. No credential or saved page-content file is read.
flow.write: In-memory leases/digests and owned browser state; image/text MCP content. No browser storage, extracted content or screenshots are persisted by the handoff registry.

flow.steps: marketplace-mcp doctor invokes selected native selfchecks sequentially and separately probes Chrome reachability; distinguish success, drift_detected and inconclusive. Every source that is not ok carries one fixed next step, chosen by a pure mapping over the per-check reasons, the static capability table, the CDP probe result and the WB transport mode. Exit 4 for a failed checker or invalid supplied subcheck, then 1 for drift, 2 for blocked/inconclusive and 0 for healthy checked sources; status-write failure is 3. diagnose_drift offers structural DOM/API diagnostics. Nightly/manual CI runs live-marked tests for WB, Detsky Mir and Yandex only; its exit-code summary does not turn blocked sources into verified health. Since 2026-11-01 the nightly job also runs the doctor round through scripts/live_check.py doctor --status-file under the shared live budget and fails on doctor alarms (exit 1 or 4), keeping blocked/inconclusive (2) green; the live-marked selfcheck tests fail on drift_detected and skip on inconclusive.
flow.read: CLI source arguments and --status-file path; source canary IDs/shape references and current upstream responses; Chrome endpoint; live test definitions. CI summary reads live.log and captured pytest exit code.
flow.write: Operator console health table with a next step under every blocked row; optional --status-file JSON (status, detail, next_step) via temporary file in target directory and atomic replacement. CI writes live.log and job summary/output. No status file is written by doctor without --status-file.

flow.steps: marketplace-mcp install resolves one unified entry for the selected profile — an absolute uv run --directory <root> <script> from a checkout, a pinned absolute-uv tool run --from ru-marketplace-mcp==__version__ entry when UV is set and sys.prefix is inside uv's cache, or the absolute console script from an ordinary wheel install — and prints it, or merges it into the client's own mcpServers file with --write: strict JSON parse, refusal (exit 2) on a malformed or conflicting file (a conflict names the configured and asked profiles), backup of the old bytes, atomic replace through a same-directory temporary file. --profile compare|decision|full selects compare-mcp (default), decision-mcp or marketplace-mcp behind the unchanged marketplace entry; --per-source keeps the per-source block and refuses --profile; claude-code prints claude mcp add command lines instead of writing; dsh keeps its cordis.patch.yml emitter and refuses --write.
flow.read: The client's own mcpServers file (Claude Desktop or Cursor), process environment, checkout path and package __version__. For uv tool environments only: UV_CACHE_DIR, or local UV cache dir subprocess output; resolve sys.prefix containment before pinning. No marketplace endpoint is contacted.
flow.write: The client configuration file, after a file.bak-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS copy of the old bytes; --dry-run writes nothing. No marketplace account, catalog or credential is touched.
flow.handoff: The client starts the unified server over stdio and reads the catalog; install itself makes no request.

flow.steps: marketplace-mcp browser status reads the CDP HTTP endpoints (/json/version, /json/list) and the browser websocket to report reachability, Chrome version, page-target count and the window state (visible, off-screen at or below -10000, minimized); it exits 1 with the start hint when the endpoint does not answer. marketplace-mcp browser show reads the first page target or the target named by unblock, un-minimizes its window, moves it on-screen (left 80, top 40, current size kept when at least 800x600, otherwise 1280x900) and activates that target. marketplace-mcp browser start [--hidden] spawns the scraping Chrome through the same loopback-only autostart code, visible by default (no off-screen arguments, nothing hidden) and with today's off-screen behaviour under --hidden; an answering CDP endpoint is reported as already running without a spawn. Both show and start send browser-level CDP commands only: no page is opened, nothing is navigated and no website is requested.
flow.read: The local CDP endpoint (/json/version, /json/list) and the browser websocket; window bounds reported by the browser. No marketplace page, credential or profile file is read.
flow.write: Window geometry and the active tab in the operator's own Chrome; console output. No file, credential or marketplace state is written.

flow.steps: marketplace-mcp unblock [sources...] [--wait SECONDS] [--dry-run] resolves named canonical sources (a non-browser source exits 2), or runs the browser-backed doctor selfchecks and takes the sources whose checks carry a WALL_REASONS reason. It starts an on-screen scraping Chrome if CDP is down, opens one new tab per source with browser-level Target.createTarget (never Page.navigate, never closing tabs), raises the window and activates the first new tab. It prints the page and the human action, waits for Enter on a TTY or --wait seconds (default 180), then re-runs only those sources' selfchecks and prints doctor's rows and next steps, with doctor's exit codes. --dry-run prints the sources and pages and does nothing else; without names it exits 2 because it would need live selfchecks. A human passes every check or login; nothing is solved, bypassed or automated.
flow.read: The local CDP endpoint, the pages in UNBLOCK_PAGES, and those sources' public pages during the re-check. No marketplace credential or profile file is read.
flow.write: New tabs and window geometry in the operator's own Chrome; console output. No file, credential or marketplace state is written.
flow.handoff: The operator passes a check or logs in; the targeted doctor-style selfchecks then report success, drift or a remaining wall.

flow.steps: marketplace-mcp setup detects Claude Desktop by its config folder, Cursor by ~/.cursor and Claude Code by claude on PATH (repeatable --client overrides detection), writes the selected profile's one-entry config through install's writer for Claude Desktop and Cursor, prints the claude mcp add line for Claude Code, reports a conflict and skips it without force, starts the scraping Chrome unless --no-browser, runs doctor's shared selfchecks/table/next steps unless --no-doctor after announcing live requests, offers unblock for walled sources on a TTY (otherwise prints the exact command) and finishes with the restart and first-question line. --dry-run prints the steps and files and writes, starts and requests nothing. Exit 0 when at least one config succeeded, 2 on bad arguments, 1 when nothing was configured and no client was found; a hard health/unblock failure overrides config success with exit 4.
flow.read: The client config folders and mcpServers files, PATH for claude/uv/console scripts, the local CDP endpoint and the selfchecks' public marketplace pages. No credential, marketplace account or unrelated file is read.
flow.write: The selected client configuration files after install's backup and atomic replace; new Chrome tabs/window geometry and console output. It never touches anything else.
flow.handoff: The operator restarts the client and asks the first comparison question; the configured server starts over stdio.

flow.source: scripts/version_sites.py; scripts/bump_version.py; scripts/check_versions.py; scripts/check_no_print.py; scripts/check_test_count.py; scripts/check_coverage_floor.py; scripts/check_lock_revision.py; .gitattributes; .github/workflows/ci.yml; .github/workflows/image-check.yml; .github/workflows/release.yml; scripts/e2e_stdio_check.py; scripts/e2e_stdio_check_docker.py
flow.steps: Root version anchors the 88 current declarations from one site table; bump_version rewrites only the matched version text, runs check_versions, then prints the relock, changelog and checklist steps it does not perform. CI declares lock/lint/types/stdout/provenance/lock-revision/schema/offline tests and 80-percent branch-coverage gates plus real stdio registration/version probes. The image-check workflow builds both Dockerfiles on relevant pull requests, drives the stdio image through a real MCP session with the root pyproject version, and runs before the release tag. .gitattributes normalizes text checkouts to LF. The lock-revision gate fails a uv.lock that an older uv rewrote as revision 3 and asks for a relock with uv >= 0.13.6. Release checks tag/version, builds all 16 workspace packages, checks distribution count/version and attaches wheels/sdists to a GitHub Release, not PyPI. These are workflow definitions, not executed outcomes of this markup change.
flow.read: scripts/version_sites.py; pyproject.toml, packages/*/pyproject.toml, packages/*/src/*/__init__.py and server.py; uv.lock; docker-compose.yml; docs/DEPLOYMENT.md; dsh/README.md; server.json; dsh/package.json; P-RELEASE notes; existing test/gate source.
flow.write: Gate diagnostics; rewritten version declarations on an explicit bump (not dry run); CI coverage artifacts; dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz during release build, plus uv's dist/.gitignore. Release upload is an external CI side effect; check_versions itself writes diagnostics only and never rewrites versions.

flow.steps: Discover root workspace patterns and member manifests; copy root release metadata, union normalized third-party base/optional requirements and scripts, drop workspace dependencies, reject mismatched specifiers/name clashes, and alias the root distribution name to marketplace-mcp. Stage declared import packages with py.typed and root README/LICENSE in a temporary hatchling project, uv build one wheel/sdist and copy them to P-PYPI. --print-pyproject writes TOML to stdout without staging/building. Additional CI installs that wheel with plain pip into a fresh non-workspace venv, runs both CLI helps and probes installed scripts. Trusted publishing is skipped until vars.PYPI_PUBLISH equals true; its pypi environment uses OIDC and verifies wheel METADATA against a selected v* tag before uploading only P-PYPI.
flow.read: Root/member pyproject.toml, packages/*/src/*, README.md and LICENSE; uv/hatchling installed build tools; wheel METADATA; owner-selected GitHub tag and variable. No marketplace endpoints or distribution-name metadata lookups.
flow.write: Temporary project and build files, ignored P-PYPI artifacts and stderr build/verdict logs; --print-pyproject builds/writes no files. CI writes a fresh venv; only a future owner-enabled publisher uploads to PyPI. Existing 16 workspace releases and Docker builds are not replaced.

flow.steps: Offline contract projection pins mounted names/arguments/output structure while excluding prose; operational stdio probes initialize and list advertised tools with bounded child cleanup. mcp_wire reports estimated wire tokens, the model-paid model_tokens (per tool and per profile the compact name, description and input schema a provider request carries, so outputSchema and annotations stay in the client), the instructions token cost the initialize result carries, and their total per profile; it compares selected profiles to the stored 10-percent budget — applied to wire_tokens and model_tokens, each against its own baseline value, with the failing measure named in the message — and to an absolute per-profile ceiling in P-WIRE. In gate mode (--baseline without --update-baseline) a missing or unreadable baseline file, an absent profile, a missing wire_tokens budget, a missing model_tokens budget or a missing positive ceiling fails the check with a clear message instead of passing silently, while measurement runs and --update-baseline stay permissive (--update-baseline keeps a ceiling already written, adds 5% above the measurement for a new profile, and writes both token measures into P-WIRE). Every budget, ceiling and threshold is read as a finite number above zero: an infinite one (1e999) bounds nothing and turns the delta into nan, a boolean is not a number, and a string is not a number either — such a value is refused with a clear message and a failing exit code, and the whole baseline file is checked, not only the profiles of this run. Routing evaluations score committed evidence/collected answers offline rather than call models.
flow.read: P-WIRE; packages/marketplace-connector/tests/fixtures/public_contract.json; registered tool schemas; work/evals/model-routing-eval.json and work/evals/routing-cases-v1.json; supplied routing answer file/stdin.
flow.write: Probe diagnostics; optional mcp_wire --update-baseline replaces P-WIRE, --json-out writes report; explicit snapshot script regeneration replaces public_contract.json. Routing report/prompt files are written only when requested. Ordinary comparison/server tool calls do not update these artifacts.

flow.steps: Import compare, decision and full profiles in-process without starting a transport; call public list_tools after output-schema compaction and list_resources, which the same servers now serve; group the tools by name prefix and render their input schemas and first description paragraph, and list each profile's resource URIs. The same measurement produces the README tools-cost blocks, so the published per-profile cost cannot drift from docs/TOOLS.md. --check renders both outputs in memory and exits 1 when either file on disk differs.
flow.read: Registered tool schemas and descriptions plus served resource URIs; README.md markers; no network, marketplace endpoint or client configuration.
flow.write: docs/TOOLS.md and the marked README blocks only when run without --check; --check writes nothing. CI runs the check in the existing lint job.

flow.steps: Captured HTML/JSON and declared SHA-256 provenance feed offline parser/extractor assertions. Optional Node/jsdom executes actual extractor source over saved markup, without live Chrome; missing tooling can skip DOM assertions. Provenance gate verifies the pinned pairs with raw/LF/CRLF normalization and reports stale exceptions, and it checks completeness: a sidecar that does not parse, carries no usable pin or describes no fixture is a failure, and so is a fixture no sidecar describes — unless the path sits in the dated KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS list with its reason (one defect per entry, a resolved entry reported so it can go).
flow.read: P-FIXTURES and declared hashes; extractor JavaScript in connector modules; Node/jsdom module resolution.
flow.write: Provenance diagnostics only; jsdom harness uses temporary runner.js and extract.js, cleaned up by its temporary-directory context. Neither gate nor ordinary offline fixture assertions recapture upstream pages or update provenance.

flow.steps: A live selfcheck, tool call or live-marked test reserves each outgoing marketplace request before sending it. The reservation loads the shared in-memory or JSON ledger, charges the request to its marketplace group, raises BudgetExhausted when the total (40) or per-marketplace (8) cap is reached, and otherwise books the request at least the configured gap (3 s) after the previous one to that group and sleeps the difference. Hooks cover httpx sync/async send, curl_cffi sync/async request, Playwright and raw-CDP page loads, in-page fetch evaluations and Ozon's subprocess hand-off; loopback CDP requests are ignored. install() validates every hook point first, and any missing point stops the run with AttributeError naming it.
flow.read: LIVE_BUDGET_TOTAL, LIVE_BUDGET_PER_SOURCE, LIVE_BUDGET_GAP_S and LIVE_BUDGET_LEDGER; the ledger JSON; the selected pytest items and their live markers.
flow.write: One stderr line per counted request; the ledger file replaced atomically; no marketplace account or content is written.
